lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Add a LinkedIn profile if you use one.
Identify whether the code link is GitHub, a portfolio, or another platform.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to identify what they’re opening.

items.says: Put experience before education.
items.because: With several years of relevant engineering experience, the work history is more important than the degree.

items.says: Put the experience entries in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Voltline is the more recent role.

items.says: Keep section formatting consistent and avoid bullets wrapping mid-phrase.
items.because: Natural line breaks make the résumé easier to scan.

items.says: Add the unit to both the 90 and 25 values.
items.because: Explicit units make the metric immediately clear.

items.says: Clarify that 20,000 units a month is the production volume covered by the test process, if accurate.
items.because: Its relationship to the time savings could be clearer.

items.says: Specify whether the lower return rate applied to the affected batch, a later run, or the overall product.
items.because: That context helps readers interpret the improvement.

items.says: Clarify what counted as a calibration drift complaint.
items.because: Complaints are less precise than a measured engineering outcome.

items.says: State the period used for the before-and-after complaint comparison.
items.because: The comparison period is unclear.

items.says: Confirm that the throughput figures use the same conditions and unit of work.
items.because: Readers need a comparable basis for the increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the throughput increase reflects a measured production rate.
items.because: The increase is strong enough that readers may want to know.

items.says: Define what update speed measures and under what conditions.
items.because: Compression and resumable downloads may affect different parts of the update process.

items.says: Add a supported result of running the HIL tests.
items.because: The bullet describes the activity but not its impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the logger identified each root cause or contributed to the diagnoses.
items.because: That distinction makes the claim more exact.

items.says: An 8 kHz sampling rate cannot capture a 5 kHz signal without aliasing.
items.because: The sampling rate must exceed twice the highest frequency of interest, with practical margin and appropriate filtering.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix the race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make access atomic or prevent a race between an interrupt handler and the main loop.

items.says: The motor-controller rewrite duplicates a nearly identical Formula Student claim.
items.because: The claim needs to belong to the right section, or the two projects must be distinguished.

items.says: Make the motor-controller work’s scope and your role unambiguous.
items.because: It is unclear what work and results belong to this role.

items.says: Clarify the before-and-after basis for the performance and fault-reduction figures.
items.because: The figures need to be credible and interpretable.

items.says: Remove the promotional “next-generation, innovation-driven” bullet.
items.because: It is not informative and does not show what you built or what changed.

items.says: Explain the basis for the power-consumption measurements.
items.because: The before-and-after figures should be measured under comparable operating conditions.

items.says: Clarify your contribution and the extent of the school’s use.
items.because: That would help show the project’s reach.

items.says: Explain what leading the 12-person team involved.
items.because: The title indicates leadership, but the bullets do not show specific responsibilities or outcomes.

items.says: Specify your personal contribution to the team’s firmware and testing.
items.because: “Worked on” is broad.

items.says: Identify your role in writing and testing the CAN-bus firmware.
items.because: The passive wording does not identify your contribution.

items.says: Clarify the dashboard and motor-controller relationship and the system’s function.
items.because: The bullet mentions both without explaining how they relate.

items.says: The 300-robot motor-control claim repeats the Voltline accomplishment.
items.because: Similar performance improvements make the duplication a major credibility risk unless the projects are distinct.

items.says: Separate the languages, microcontroller platform, and lab equipment in the Tools category.
items.because: The current category mixes different types of skills.

items.says: Separate technical practices from the CAN protocol in the Methods category.
items.because: The current category mixes different types of skills.

items.says: Remove or narrow “firmware” as a standalone skill.
items.because: It describes a field of work rather than a distinct skill.

items.says: Add other relevant embedded tools, languages, or debugging and build systems if accurate.
items.because: The experience suggests you may have used technologies not listed in Skills.
